frames.narration: t=0. Worker A asks the lease service for the right to write the shared file. It gets a 10 second lease and fencing token 1.
t=1. A writes A1 and attaches token 1. The file has not seen any token yet, so it accepts and remembers 1 as the highest token.
t=3. A checks its lease (valid until t=10) and starts the next step. Then a garbage collection pause freezes the whole process until t=18. A cannot renew and cannot notice time passing.
t=10. The lease expires and the service grants it to Worker B with a higher token, 2. The service did the right thing: it cannot tell a frozen holder from a dead one.
t=10. B writes B1 with token 2. The file accepts it and raises its highest seen token to 2.
t=18. A wakes up. Its local state still says the lease is valid, so two workers now believe they own the file. A sends its next write, still carrying token 1.
If the file does not check tokens it accepts A2 and overwrites B's newer data. The two owners have corrupted the file, and nothing on the client side could have prevented it.
If the file checks tokens it sees 1 is lower than the 2 it has already seen, and rejects A2. A learns it lost the lease and must re-acquire. The stale owner is harmless.
